protocol.scope: Measure before choosing a production change. Preserve terminal drain, final output, hook order, raw/alternate-screen restoration, shared shutdown and actual owned process/VM release. No forced early exit, guessed process kill, foreign VM deletion or timeout increase.
priorV: PF02 bundled/fullscreen quit timing baseline band 10.151%
FSEventWrap in pre-exit snapshot may be async close pending, not owner leak
hypotheses: Idle 50ms drain is intentional terminal protocol protection; do not remove it for benchmark speed
Active provider/tool cancellation currently starts after drain and UI stop; phase probe must establish user-visible delay and any safe overlap before changing ordering
Track watcher close request versus close event in a separate natural-exit diagnostic child to classify pre-exit FSEventWrap
coverage: idle/active stream/cooperative tool and real child command
compaction/branch summary, MCP, slow/failed extension, repeated close/startup cancellation
backpressure/slow or disconnected output, both renderers, print/RPC
actual Windows Sandbox offline/online paths and tools, explicit cancellation of owned active VM operation before joining close
protocol.measurement: Five independent processes with 30 formal observations for any timing claim; raw phase timings separate from uninstrumented totals. Same-machine paired control if code changes. PF00 threshold max(5%, max absolute process-p95 deviation from median), >10% baseline band requires diagnosis. Existing regression suite results may be reused only for identical source; new boundary tests and relevant allocation/lifecycle gates required for production changes.
protocol.environment: Windows host exposes WindowsSandbox.exe; existing opt-in workspace test uses pwsh7 and fixed public is-number@7.0.0 install with scripts disabled. Fresh isolated project and artifacts under this task TMP. Network enabled only in explicit enabled arm. No credentials/real user config/paid provider.
protocol.limits: Native terminal latency and real provider cancellation not inferred from pipe/alpha fixtures. A backend close is documented to join pending work; caller must revoke/cancel its execution boundary first. Do not call close alone and treat deliberate join semantics as a cancellation bug.

Use run.mjs with isolated HOME. The reduced baseline-files manifest overlays only workspace-backend, the sole production change; other pre-edit snapshot hashes are audit-only. import assert from 'node:assert/strict';import {tmpdir} from 'node:os';import fs from 'node:fs';import path from 'node:path';import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';const root=fs.realpathSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('.',import.meta.url)));assert.equal(fs.realpathSync(tmpdir()),root);for(const key of ['TMP','TEMP','TMPDIR'])assert.equal(fs.realpathSync(process.env[key]),root);fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root,'env-'+process.pid+'.json'),JSON.stringify({pid:process.pid,tmpdir:tmpdir(),time:new Date().toISOString()}));
const receipt=path.join(root,'env-'+process.pid+'.json');function recordExit(code){const info=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(receipt,'utf8'));info.closed=new Date().toISOString();info.exitCode=code;fs.writeFileSync(receipt,JSON.stringify(info));}process.on('exit',recordExit);

limitations: Pipe-backed timing is not native terminal latency; phase probe changes import order.
Runtime-dispose relative p95 band 10.4821% at about 5ms; no stable subphase latency claim.
One isolated admission timing candidate outlier; no absolute nanosecond timing claim.
Live active test proves physical exec CLI in flight, not guest command entry.
Outer cleanup retry does not override the underlying VM blocked-cleanup policy.
